title: Research notes: Chambers Site (15Ml109)
summary: Sources for the upland Mississippian village at Chambers, Marshall County. Pin generalized to 0.1° at the county center; occupation years from radiocarbon dates, not the 1980s excavation.

items.text: Large upland village in Marshall County; about 6 ha; a stone-box cemetery was reported at the site.
Recorded in the mid-1980s; Pollack and Railey 1987 report.
Calibrated radiocarbon dates suggest occupation AD 1250–1350; Angelly phase by its handles.
Two wall-trench houses (5 × 6.4 m; 6 × 8 m), trash area 10 × 16 m, over 1 m of deposits with prepared floors and midden.
Terrace/bench interpretation (Pollack and Railey) vs. edge of a platform mound (Clay 1997).
Maize, nutshell, maygrass; less fish (5%) than river sites, no migratory birds; Dover and Mill Creek chert hoes.
Pans 17% vs. 6% at Adams; bowls 16% vs. 37%.
Deer hunting (in the brief) is not stated in the source pages read, so it was cut.

openQuestions: Whether the prepared floors are the edge of a platform mound.

sources.citation: David Pollack, ed., The Archaeology of Kentucky: An Update, vol. 2 (Kentucky Heritage Council, 2008), Mississippi Period chapter, pp. 629–633.
